suggestions.rationale: Clinical Mapping Master Batch 2026 publishes this relationship only as complication outcome risk. Require established Charcot foot/lower-extremity neuropathic arthropathy and a documented subsequent lower-extremity amputation outcome. Long-term Charcot-foot cohort supports amputation risk/limb preservation only; do not generalize this source to generic loss of use or non-foot Charcot arthropathy. The cited literature supports only this bounded proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-10 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Charcot neuroarthropathy can progress to foot deformity and ulceration, creating a clinically recognized pathway to deep infection and osteomyelitis; use of this relationship requires documented wound or infection chronology. Require established Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot plus documented deformity with ulceration, soft-tissue breakdown, wound infection, or compatible deep-infection chronology before using the osteomyelitis pathway. Osteomyelitis must be separately diagnosed. Preserve diabetes, neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, trauma or surgery, wound-care history, and other infection risk factors. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
